instruction: Parametric Row of Through-Holes `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` holds a single mesh object named `Plate`: a rectangular slab aligned to the world axes. Read the scene to determine the plate's exact dimensions and origin. Drill through-bores in the plate so the saved output satisfies every requirement below. Save the completed scene as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Requirements 1. Scene contains exactly one mesh object, still named `Plate`, with its world location and rotation unchanged from the input. 2. The plate's outer envelope (top face, bottom face, four side faces) is preserved; only internal material is removed. 3. Five cylindrical through-bores of diameter 0.20 BU pierce the plate vertically (bore axis ‖ world Z), from top face to bottom face. 4. All five bore axes lie on the plate's mid-span Y line (Y = plate_center_Y). 5. The five bore centers are equispaced along X and leave equal end margins on both sides of the plate's X extent. 6. The final mesh is closed and manifold: every edge bounded by exactly two faces; no loose vertices; no non-manifold edges. Inspect before acting — the plate's exact X length determines where the bores go. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. In this image, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.
